document_metadata.doc_title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin, a twelve-year-old with an aged appearance, helps a blind, elderly woman and her dog settle in, though he cannot recall her name, reflecting on how forgotten people can leave a lasting impact.
document_metadata.source_title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: Benjamin sitting at a table, an old man to look at but no more than twelve, busy playing with magnets... BENJAMIN (V.O) Until... We see a refined, genteel OLD WOMAN, wearing a hat and gloves, a suitcase at her feet, flanked by an old DOG, just inside the front door... BENJAMIN (CONT'D) Hello... THE WOMAN I'm moving in today. And just then Queenie appears, the baby on her hip... QUEENIE Welcome... we was expecting you... (to Benjamin) Could you show her upstairs? (MORE) . CONTINUED: QUEENIE (CONT'D) She will be staying in Mrs. Rousseau's old room. I'll be right with you with some fresh towels... (frowning) We don't usually let dogs in the house.

metadata.doc_title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.summary: Benjamin, a twelve-year-old with an aged appearance, helps a blind, elderly woman and her dog settle in, though he cannot recall her name, reflecting on how forgotten people can leave a lasting impact.
metadata.source_title: 67、INT. FRONT ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: THE WOMAN He's as old as the hills. Blind too. Can hardly get around, he won't be a bother much longer. Benjamin, like any young boy, immediately pets the old dog... QUEENIE I guess as long as he stays out from underfoot. Benjamin helps her with her bags showing her up the stairs...the old dog dutifully following them... BENJAMIN I'm Benjamin... The woman starts to tell him her name... but we don't hear it because...BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (after a beat) As hard as I try, I can't remember her name. Mrs. Lawson, or Mrs. Hartford, or maybe it was Maple? It's funny how sometimes the people we remember the least, make the greatest impression on us.

document_metadata.source_title: 68、INT. THE OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,

chunks.content: Benjamin sits petting the dog while the Woman puts her things away... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) I remember she wore diamonds... and she always dressed in fine clothing as if she was going out. Although, she never did and nobody would ever come to visit her. .

document_metadata.title: 69、INT. NOLAN HOUSE, PARLOR - VISITING DAY,

chunks.content: We see the Woman dressed nicely, sitting in a chair reading a book. She takes a look out the window at the families on the lawn and bends back to her book. BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) ...She taught me how to play the piano...

document_metadata.doc_title: 70、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 70、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin learns piano from a woman who teaches him that emotion matters more than skill, guiding him from classical to ragtime music, which he connects with deeply.
document_metadata.source_title: 70、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER NIGHT,

chunks.content: The Woman sitting with Benjamin teaching him how to play piano...playing a classical piece like Chopin...Benjamin trying his hand...sounding pretty bad... THE WOMAN It isn't how well you play, it's how you feel about what you're playing. (whispers) Try this. And she plays a ragtime piece...New Orleans music...music for the other whole part of the soul... Benjamin tries his hand and actually plays it fairly well THE WOMAN (CONT'D) You cannot help but put your entire self into the music. And he plays along with her...a piece he won't soon forget... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) There were many changes going on, some you could see... some you couldn't.

document_metadata.doc_title: 71、INT. A BATHROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 71、INT. A BATHROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin notices physical changes like gray hair and underarm hair, observes his maturing body in the mirror, and feels a sense of empowerment and masculinity as he flexes his muscles.
document_metadata.source_title: 71、INT. A BATHROOM, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin taking a bath. An he notices a single gray hair floating on the surface... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) Hair, had started growing, in all sorts of places... And he sees some hair is under his arms... and as he looks downward... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) Along with other things... . CONTINUED: Benjamin, naked, looking at himself in a mirror... like a young teenage boy... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) I felt like I could do anything, that I could sprout wings... And as he flexes his muscles, feeling like a man.

document_metadata.doc_title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT
document_metadata.title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT
document_metadata.summary: Daisy briefly opens her eyes, sharing a quiet moment with Caroline, who begins reading before Daisy closes her eyes as Benjamin's voice narrates a memory of boat trips with Mr. Daws.
document_metadata.source_title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

chunks.content: It's started to rain, the wind blowing, splattering rain against the window. Knocking. DAISY Oh, darlin', the pain... CAROLINE I'll get the nurse... She hurries out of the room. Daisy looks out the window. The maelstrom of wind and rain. Caroline comes back with a Nurse. THE NURSE You're not feeling too good? She adjusts the morphine drip. Daisy lays back. THE NURSE (CONT'D) Nobody seems to know whether to stay or leave. The roads are filled from New Orleans to Baton Rouge already. I think I'm gonna ride it out. (finishing with the drip) There, that should make things easier. Daisy starts to feel the effects of the drip... THE NURSE (CONT'D) (to Caroline) Have you had a chance to say your goodbyes? Caroline nods. The Nurse nods. THE NURSE (CONT'D) My father waited four hours for my brother to get here from Boger City. He couldn't go without him. She affectionately touches Daisy's cheek. THE NURSE (CONT'D) She seems like a sweet woman. Caroline nods. CAROLINE I haven't spent as much time as I would have like with her the last few years.

metadata.doc_title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT
metadata.title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

metadata.source_title: 72、INT. HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

chunks.content: Another NURSE looks in... THE WOMAN You busy? The Nurse quickly goes out of the room. Caroline sits back down looking at her mother... Daisy opens her eyes... they look at each other... Caroline knowing Daisy wants to hear the sound of her voice... CAROLINE (taking up the book) The next page says... Daisy shuts her eyes...BENJAMIN (V.O.) ...Queenie would let me go with Mr. Daws to Bridge City..To watch the boats go up and down the river...

document_metadata.doc_title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,
document_metadata.title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin eagerly takes a job on Capt. Mike's tugboat despite warnings about unpaid wages, proving willing to work when others hesitate.
document_metadata.source_title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,

chunks.content: The busy docks... Men waiting, hoping to find work... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) These were hard times... people were doing anything they could to find work... And we see Benjamin, with Mr. Daws, \"the lightning man,\" sitting on a bench with a line of other old men, \"killing time,\" watching the boats going up and down the River... MR. DAWS Did I ever tell you I was struck by lightning seven times? Once, when I was in a field tending to my cows. And we see just that, Mr. Daws, along with a cow of his, being hit by lightning. A MAN'S (V.O.) (shouts) My fourt' hand didn't show up... Anybody want to make $2 for a day's work around here... Benjamin turns... And he sees a man in his late 40s with his three man crew, standing on the deck of a TUGBOAT, and old rusted tug built out of charcoal iron... The man, its Captain MIKE... Has a thick Irish accent... For some reason none of the able-bodied men needing work respond...

metadata.doc_title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,
metadata.title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,
metadata.summary: Benjamin eagerly takes a job on Capt. Mike's tugboat despite warnings about unpaid wages, proving willing to work when others hesitate.
metadata.source_title: 73、EXT. THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - DAY,

chunks.content: CAPT. MIKE What's wrong, nobody wants to get their hands dirty...! Nobody wants to do an honest days work for an honest day's pay...! A MAN (warning them) He never pays... He always says he'll have to owe it to you... . CONTINUED: CAPT. MIKE Are all you afraid of workin' for a livin'? Somebody got to want a job... Benjamin suddenly springs up at the opportunity, waving his arms... BENJAMIN I do...! CAPT. MIKE You got your sea legs old man? BENJAMIN (feeling his legs) I do. I think. CAPT. MIKE That's good enough for me! Get your ass on board, we'll sure as hell find out!And as Benjamin gets on the boat, heading out to sea...

document_metadata.doc_title: 74、EXT. TUGBOAT, MISSISSIPPI RIVER, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,
document_metadata.title: 74、EXT. TUGBOAT, MISSISSIPPI RIVER, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin is eager to work on the boat and will be paid for his tasks; Captain Mike Clark, his employer, has extensive boating experience since childhood.
document_metadata.source_title: 74、EXT. TUGBOAT, MISSISSIPPI RIVER, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,

chunks.content: And we see Benjamin "learning the ropes..." Helping to tow the freighters, into and out of the River ports... Benjamin in this element, like a boy, his hair blowing, thrilled to be on the boat, thrilled by the adventure... willing to do anything... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) I was as happy as I could be... I would do anything... CAPT. MIKE I needs a volunteah. BENJAMIN Yes, Captain! CAPT. MIKE (motioning) Scrape off this bird shit. BENJAMIN Right away, sir...! And he hops to it... Happily scraping off the bird shit... Happy to be doing anything...

metadata.doc_title: 74、EXT. TUGBOAT, MISSISSIPPI RIVER, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,

chunks.content: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) And I actually was going to be paid for something I would have done for free. CAPT. MIKE I'll put you on the books... pay you next time around...BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) His name was Captain Mike Clark... He'd been on boats since he was seven...

document_metadata.doc_title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Captain Mike, shocked by Benjamin's admission of never having been with a woman, invites him along to meet some friends, prompting a new experience.
document_metadata.source_title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: Mike's a hard drinker, God's last angry man... He's drinking as they go in for the night... Benjamin sitting with him in the wheelhouse... Capt. Mike jawing away... CAPT. MIKE ... What were you born to do, old timer? BENJAMIN I haven't found out yet. CAPT. MIKE You haven't found out yet?! How old are you, Benjamin, seventy somethin' or other? BENJAMIN Not as old as I look. CAPT. MIKE (laughs) Tha's a good one...\" You older than Hades you creaky old bastard! What the hell you been doing with your life? BENJAMIN It's a short story...

metadata.doc_title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.summary: Captain Mike, shocked by Benjamin's admission of never having been with a woman, invites him along to meet some friends, prompting a new experience.
metadata.source_title: 75、INT. TUGBOAT WHEELHOUSE - END OF ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: CAPT. MIKE Can you still get it up? BENJAMIN (doesn't understand) I do every morning. . CONTINUED: CAPT. MIKE The old pole? The hard'n? Can you still get it up? BENJAMIN (not so sure) I guess. CAPT. MIKE When was the last time you had a woman, you creaky old bastard...? BENJAMIN Never. CAPT. MIKE Never! BENJAMIN Not that I know of. CAPT. MIKE (can't believe his ears) You been on this earth for more than seventy years and you never got any?! That's the saddest thing I ever heard in my life. Never?BENJAMIN Never. CAPT. MIKE Well, then, hell man, you comin' with me!! BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) He took me to meet some friends...

document_metadata.doc_title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Capt. Mike, a tugboat captain, deflects Benjamin's observation about his job, then offers him an experience as education, implying its value surpasses monetary payment.
document_metadata.source_title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,

chunks.content: Music playing loud... We see Benjamin and Capt Mike at the bar... Mike, hammered... CAPT. MIKE You din't say? What did your father do? BENJAMIN I never met my father. . CONTINUED: CAPT. MIKE You're a lucky bastard! All father's want to do is hold you down!.. Out on my father's boat, working da two-a-days... This littl' fat bastard, \"tug Irish,\" what they calls them. They say the Irish the only one's stupid `nough to work a tug. Them and the Portuguese, as we all know how stupid them Portuguese is. I fin'ly get up the nerves and tell him... \"I don't wanta spend da rest of my life on a goddamn tugboat...!\" You know what I'm sayin'? BENJAMIN You didn't want to spend the rest of your life on a tugboat. CAPT. MIKE Absolutely, damn right! So you know what my father says? He says \"Who the hell you think you are?\" \"What the hell you think you can do?\" I tell him. \"Well if you askin' -- I want to be a artist.\" He laughs. He says, \"If God wanted you to be an artist he would made you one.\" \"God wanted you to work a tugboat just like me, and that's what you goin' to do?\" \"Now, if I ever hear you mention art again, I'll throw you overboard!\" Well, I went and I show him... I made myself an artist... And he suddenly takes off his shirt, pulls down his pants... And we see he's covered, from head to toe, with \"his artwork,\" and incredible array of tattoos... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) A tattoos artist...! I puts every one on myself! And they look it, upside down sideways and backwards... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) You have to skin me alive to take my art away from me now! When I'm dead I'm going to send him my arm! (MORE) . CONTINUED: CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) Don't let anyone tell you different! You got to do what you meant to do! And I happen to be a god-damned artist!

metadata.doc_title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,

metadata.source_title: 76、INT. A CLUB, THE FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,

chunks.content: BENJAMIN (stating the obvious) But you're a tugboat captain. Which stops Captain Mike in mid rant... And he has no answer for... His only response is to glare at Benjamin... A back door opens, a slinky woman coming in... THE WOMAN Captain Mike, we're ready for you and your friend... CAPT. MIKE Let's go old timer... Break your cherry... This one's on me... As they go... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) (reconsidering) And here's you pay for today... Don't ever let anybody tell you Captain Mike didn't give a man what he deserved...BENJAMIN (looks at change he was given) I thought it was $2 for a day's work... CAPT. MIKE \"you can't put a price on education...\"

document_metadata.source_title: 79、INT. THE ROOM, WHORE HOUSE, FRENCH QUARTER - NIGHT,

chunks.content: She's pushing him down, hiking up her skirt, all business... THE GIRL Let's go... Time's a wastin'... She climbs on top of him... And instinct takes over... But Benjamin being just a boy... and this being the first time, his excitement gets the immediate best of him... BENJAMIN Ohhh...! THE GIRL (hopping up) Come by anytime... She starts to leave... But Benjamin, who likes this an awful lot... BENJAMIN Again? . CONTINUED: THE GIRL Again? She looks and sees, sure enough... She climbs back on...the results are virtually the same if a bit longer THE GIRL (CONT'D) My hat's off to you old timer.She gets up to go... she's made it to the door... when Benjamin says... BENJAMIN Again? THE GIRL Again? She slows, turns to look... And sure enough... He's as ready as he's ever going to be... As she looks at him, a look bordering on amazement...

chunks.content: And we see Benjamin, at the door, happily smiling... BENJAMIN Thank you... THE GIRL (hurting) No, thank you... Benjamin, floating on air, hovering, never wants to leave... THE GIRL (CONT'D) Have a nice night... . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN You'll be here tomorrow? THE GIRL Every night, but Sunday... And she's finally able to go... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) It sure made me understand the value of earning a living... the things it can buy you.. Benjamin turns to leave... we hear footsteps... And we see a man, putting on a raincoat, coming downstairs from one of those other rooms...

document_metadata.title: 84、INT. BAR, FRENCH QUARTER - LATE AT NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin reveals he was born with a condition making him appear old, discusses his adoption, and shares a drink with Thomas, who apologizes for his disease as they bond over whiskey.
document_metadata.source_title: 84、INT. BAR, FRENCH QUARTER - LATE AT NIGHT,

chunks.content: A small old bar. Benjamin and his father sitting in the back... The waiter comes over, deferring to Benjamin's age... THE WAITER What will it be sir? BENJAMIN I'll have whatever he's having. THOMAS BUTTON A Sazerac for both of us...with whiskey instead of brandy... The waiter leaves. THOMAS BUTTON (CONT'D) You don't drink do you? BENJAMIN It's a night for firsts... THOMAS BUTTON How is that? BENJAMIN I've never been to a whore house either. THOMAS BUTTON It's an... experience... BENJAMIN It certainly is. (and honestly) I'm not very experienced about a lot of things. THOMAS BUTTON That isn't a bad thing. BENJAMIN There's a first time for everything.

metadata.doc_title: 84、INT. BAR, FRENCH QUARTER - LATE AT NIGHT,
metadata.title: 84、INT. BAR, FRENCH QUARTER - LATE AT NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Benjamin reveals he was born with a condition making him appear old, discusses his adoption, and shares a drink with Thomas, who apologizes for his disease as they bond over whiskey.
metadata.source_title: 84、INT. BAR, FRENCH QUARTER - LATE AT NIGHT,

chunks.content: THOMAS BUTTON True enough. I don't mean to be rude... but your hands seem awful bent... It must be quite painful? BENJAMIN I don't really know what I have. I have some form of a disease. I have a lot of catching up to do. THOMAS BUTTON What kind of a disease? BENJAMIN I was born old. Thomas is quiet. And for many things... THOMAS BUTTON I'm sorry. BENJAMIN (guileless) No need to be. Nothing wrong with old age. THOMAS BUTTON I'm sorry about your disease. BENJAMIN My mother says we're all born with something... THOMAS BUTTON Your mother? BENJAMIN I'm adopted. Thomas looks at him... They get their drinks... Tap glasses, and drink.Benjamin coughs at the taste... But forces it down... And as they laugh at his discomfort...

document_metadata.doc_title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Thomas reveals he makes buttons, competes with zippers; Benjamin, a tugboat worker, offers to pay for another drink, showing pride in his work.
document_metadata.source_title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,

chunks.content: Thomas and Benjamin are deep in conversation, both more than a few sheets to the wind, with Benjamin especially overblown like any first-time drunk. Thomas Button reveals, 'My wife passed away many years ago... She died in childbirth.' There's a moment when it seems like he might say more, but despite the alcohol, he thinks better of it. Instead, he toasts sadly, 'To children,' and Benjamin, nodding, responds, 'To mothers and fathers,' clinking glasses in shared sentiment.

metadata.doc_title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,
metadata.title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Thomas reveals he makes buttons, competes with zippers; Benjamin, a tugboat worker, offers to pay for another drink, showing pride in his work.
metadata.source_title: 85、INT. THE BAR - FRENCH QUARTER - LATER THAT NIGHT,

chunks.content: After a pause, Benjamin asks, 'What line of work are you in, Mr. Button?' Thomas replies, 'Buttons. "Button's Buttons." There isn't a button we don't make. Our biggest competition is B.F. Goodrich and his infernal zippers.' The waiter approaches and asks if they'd like another drink. Thomas turns to Benjamin, 'One more, Benjamin?' Benjamin, eager to contribute, offers, 'If you'll let me pay for it, Mr. Button,' pulling out a small amount of his hard-earned pay with pride.Thomas, noticing the gesture, asks, 'What kind of work do you do?' Benjamin, still proud, responds, 'I'm a tugboat man.'

document_metadata.source_title: 86、EXT. NOLAN HOUSE - LATE AT NIGHT,

chunks.content: The car's stopped outside the gate... Benjamin is drunkenly getting out... THOMAS BUTTON I enjoyed talking to you... BENJAMIN I enjoyed drinking with you... He starts to wobble inside... THOMAS BUTTON (after him) Benjamin... Benjamin slows... THOMAS BUTTON (CONT'D) Would you mind, if time to time, I stopped by to say hello...? BENJAMIN (a drunken wave) Anytime. THOMAS BUTTON (happily) Goodnight, Benjamin. BENJAMIN (drunkenly) Absolutely... Mr. Button... Benjamin turns inside. Thomas looks after him for a long moment... And then he drives away...

BENJAMIN I think he has mejembe. (shaking him) Captain Mike... could you take us out? Captain Mike opens one eye... sees them standing there... CAPT. MIKE You know what day it is? BENJAMIN Sunday. CAPT. MIKE Do you know what dat mean? He doesn't. CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) It means I was very drunk last night. BENJAMIN You're drunk every night.

document_metadata.source_title: 93、EXT. THE TUGBOAT, THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER - EARLY,

chunks.content: The tugboat making its way through the fog... Benjamin standing with Daisy on the prow... the wind in their faces... And suddenly out of the fog a HORN BLARES... As loud as anything they have ever heard... and moving out of the mist, horn still echoing, a huge ocean liner appears... With three other tugboats pushing it to sea... CAPT. MIKE She put in for repair... a wounded duck... She's flyin' now... Captain Mike joins the tugs at the liner's side... the tugs sounding horns of their own... a symphony of a kind... What interests Benjamin... BENJAMIN What does it take to build something like that?

document_metadata.doc_title: 94、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT
document_metadata.title: 94、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT
document_metadata.summary: Caroline cares for her unresponsive mother Daisy, who murmurs in confusion. Amid the storm, Caroline continues reading aloud as Daisy seems unaware she had stopped, reflecting their strained, repetitive routine.
document_metadata.source_title: 94、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

chunks.content: The rain and wind knocking at the window... DAISY (murmurs) I wish we could have... (the morphine) CAROLINE Did you say something, Mother? And there's a hint of anxiety in Caroline now... anxiety coupled with exhaustion... Daisy doesn't say anything. Caroline worriedly looks out the window. CAROLINE (CONT'D) It seems to be getting worse. Daisy doesn't respond. CAROLINE (CONT'D) Are you hearing me, mother? DAISY Look at that... time just seeped out of me... CAROLINE What? DAISY Somebody will come and mop it up and that will be the end... Caroline can only listen... She takes a deep breath, gathering her strength...

document_metadata.doc_title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin's arrogance about reversing aging fades as a friend reveals the emotional burden of outliving loved ones, reshaping his view on life, loss, and their meaning.
document_metadata.source_title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin's REFLECTION in a mirror... WE PULL BACK TO SEE we're in his friend's room... Benjamin sitting in a straight back chair, getting a haircut, the dog at their feet, the VICTROLA, as usual, is working overtime. The woman, someone he doesn’t know well, observes him and remarks with gentle irony that he seems to have more hair than before. Benjamin, feeling a bit self-assured, responds with a provocative thought: what if he weren’t aging like everyone else—but instead, growing younger? His tone carries a hint of arrogance, as if this reversal were a gift or a clever secret.

metadata.doc_title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,
metadata.summary: Benjamin's arrogance about reversing aging fades as a friend reveals the emotional burden of outliving loved ones, reshaping his view on life, loss, and their meaning.
metadata.source_title: 95、INT. OLDER WOMAN'S ROOM - NOLAN HOUSE - ANOTHER DAY,

chunks.content: But her reply cuts through his pride. She says she’d feel sorry for him—to have to watch everyone he loves die before his eyes. The comment silences him; it’s a perspective he’s never considered. The weight of immortality, or reversed aging, suddenly feels less like a miracle and more like a burden. She continues, calling it an awful responsibility, one that isolates as much as it preserves. In that moment, Benjamin is still, truly listening.And seeing his distress, she offers a quiet, profound truth: 'Benjamin... We’re meant to lose the people we love. How else would we know how important they are to us.' Her words linger in the air, reshaping his understanding of life and loss. Benjamin Button's voiceover reflects that he had never thought about life or death that way before. And one fall day... a familiar visitor came knocking on our door...

chunks.content: We see Benjamin knocking on the Woman's door... BENJAMIN Would you like to go for a walk? There's no response. He opens it, going inside... The Woman is sitting in a chair by the window, the dog at her feet, the familiar Victrola playing dance music... He comes around the chair. And he sees she's still... perfectly still... her soul moved on... .

document_metadata.title: 99、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin says goodbye to elders, aware he may never see them again, while young Daisy watches silently from afar, avoiding farewell.
document_metadata.source_title: 99、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - DAY,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin moving through the parlor, one by one, saying his good-byes to the old people... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) I knew, life being what it was, I would probably never see them again... The familiar faces... And as we watch him affectionately touch or talk to each of them... we can just see out a screen window DAISY, almost thirteen now, leaning against the side of the house... Out of sight... as if she didn't say goodbye, he wouldn't leave... .

document_metadata.doc_title: 100、EXT. THE FRONT PORCH - NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,
document_metadata.title: 100、EXT. THE FRONT PORCH - NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin leaves for sea as Daisy runs away, overwhelmed; he watches her go, then departs, vowing to send postcards from everywhere.
document_metadata.source_title: 100、EXT. THE FRONT PORCH - NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,

chunks.content: We see TIZZY on the porch holding Benjamin's suitcase for him... The woman's old dog lying beside him... TIZZY (shaking his hand) Good luck, son. And we see Queenie has come out onto the porch with her little girl... and he holds Queenie... tears running down her face... BENJAMIN Goodbye, Mother... He bends to pet the old dog goodbye... He takes up his suitcase and starts off the porch... going down the walkway... he hesitates, and opens the gate... moving out onto the street... When suddenly Daisy is calling him... DAISY Benjamin... Benjamin... She comes running. He stops to let her catch up to him... DAISY (CONT'D) Where are you going? BENJAMIN To sea. I'll send you a postcard.

metadata.doc_title: 100、EXT. THE FRONT PORCH - NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,
metadata.title: 100、EXT. THE FRONT PORCH - NOLAN HOUSE - DAY,

chunks.content: DAISY From everywhere. Write me a postcard from everywhere... And with so much she wants to say, she can't say anything. So she runs away... He watches her go, watches her thin legs running back down the street... and he turns and moves off along the street... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) And I went off to sea...

document_metadata.source_title: 101、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

chunks.content: Daisy's quiet. Caroline can't avoid the howling of the wind. . CONTINUED: CAROLINE (concerned) I think I should find out what's going on... DAISY (stops her) There's a box of them... in a velvet bag... Caroline, not sure what she wants, opens a red velvet bag... she finds a wooden cigar box... CAROLINE Is this what you're looking for? DAISY Looking for? CAROLINE You said you wanted this? DAISY Of course. She gives her the box... Daisy, opens it... It's filled with postcards...

metadata.doc_title: 101、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

Daisy, the postcards, fond memories spread out on the bed around her... DAISY (CONT'D) Please keep reading, sugar... Caroline takes another look at the window, then takes up the book...CAROLINE (sitting back down) \"I had gone..\" -71. CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) \"... With Captain Mike's crew on the \"Chelsea\"...\"

chunks.content: Daisy reading the very postcard some sixty odd years later... as if reading it for the first time... DAISY \"...I've met somebody...and I've fallen in love...\" My, that was over... (and realizing) ...sixty years ago. She's quiet, looking out the window... CAROLINE Did you love him, mother? DAISY What can a girl know about love? document_metadata.title: 114、EXT. MURMANSK HARBOR, RUSSIA - DAY,

document_metadata.source_title: 114、EXT. MURMANSK HARBOR, RUSSIA - DAY,

chunks.content: We see "Chelsea" working with other tugs as snow falls in the crowded Russian Harbor. They tow a large freighter into port. CAPT. MIKE Benjamin... Benjamin, who is coiling rope on the bow, stands and looks at the Captain. CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) (squinting down at him, wanting to know) Tell me how's it happen you showed up you were no bigger than a bollard. Now either I drink a helluva lot more than I think I do, or you sprouted... What's your secret?

metadata.doc_title: 114、EXT. MURMANSK HARBOR, RUSSIA - DAY,
metadata.title: 114、EXT. MURMANSK HARBOR, RUSSIA - DAY,

chunks.content: And Benjamin, tired of explanations, and what comes first to mind... BENJAMIN Well Captain, you do drink a lot... And that makes perfect sense to Mike... CAPT. MIKE (taking a drink, saluting) Goddamn right I do! And Benjamin stands on the bow... ready to see the world...BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) We stayed at a small hotel with the grand name, "The Winter Palace."

document_metadata.doc_title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Captain Mike, drunk, explains hummingbird wings' figure-eight pattern symbolizing infinity; the bar laughs, united in drunkenness. The Brody twins start fighting again.
document_metadata.source_title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: There's a packed BAR off the lobby where Benjamin sits with Captain Mike, their crew, and a mix of seamen from various backgrounds—Russians and others—crowded around tables cluttered with bottles and glasses. Captain Mike, drunk and shirtless, passionately tells a Russian sailor about a tattoo he has over his heart: an upside-down hummingbird. Through an interpreter, he explains that he saw the tattoo in Singapore, done by Sakumoro, the greatest tattoo artist who ever lived, and tried to recreate it from memory—hence its inverted position. He insists it’s no ordinary bird: its heart beats twelve hundred times a minute, its wings flap eighty times per second, and if they stop, the bird dies within ten seconds. He calls it a miracle.

metadata.doc_title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Captain Mike, drunk, explains hummingbird wings' figure-eight pattern symbolizing infinity; the bar laughs, united in drunkenness. The Brody twins start fighting again.
metadata.source_title: 116、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: Captain Mike continues, animated, explaining how scientists slowed down footage of hummingbird wings using moving pictures, revealing that the wingtips trace a figure-eight pattern. He grabs a napkin and draws the shape emphatically, then asks the group if they know what the figure-eight symbolizes in mathematics. Pausing for effect, he points at the drawing and shouts, 'Infinity!' Despite the language barriers, the room erupts in laughter, united by the absurdity and the alcohol. Benjamin Button’s voiceover reflects on this moment, observing that no matter their differences—language, skin color, origin—everyone in that bar shared one undeniable trait: they were drunk every single night.Then there's a shout—and as if to underscore things, the Brody twins are kicking the shit out of each other again...

document_metadata.doc_title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth Abbott, embarrassed about breaking her shoe heel, walks barefoot down the hall with dignity while Benjamin observes, recalling the moment as part of long, memorable days.
document_metadata.source_title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin waiting for the small caged elevator to take him to his room. He gets in, the elevator operator about to shut the grill door... A WOMAN'S (V.O.) Would you wait, please... And we see a WOMAN in her late 40s... getting on the elevator... Benjamin looks over at her... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) Her name was Elizabeth Abbott. She was not beautiful. She was plain as paper... But she was as pretty as any picture to me... "Plain as paper," ELIZABETH ABBOTT... Directly behind her walks a tall, tired man, in his 50s... By the look of his ruddy face, and her silent mien... they're both drunk... Benjamin finds himself looking at her... . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT What are you looking at? She has a distinctly English accent. Benjamin doesn't say a word. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) If you must know, we have a long standing agreement never to go to bed sober. Isn't that right darling? BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) Her husband was Walter Abbott...He was Chief Minister of the British Trade Mission in Murmansk... and he was a spy...

metadata.doc_title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Elizabeth Abbott, embarrassed about breaking her shoe heel, walks barefoot down the hall with dignity while Benjamin observes, recalling the moment as part of long, memorable days.
metadata.source_title: 117、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: They ride up. Elizabeth has her shoes off...She sees him noting her stocking feet... The elevator finally rattles to a stop, and George and Elizabeth get off... Starting down the hall...she abruptly turns to say to Benjamin... so that it's completely understood... ELIZABETH ABBOTT I broke the heel off of one of my shoes...I don't usually walk around in my bare feet... And as he watches her saunter along the hallway... the way drunks do... endeavoring to keep her dignity... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) They were long days there...

document_metadata.doc_title: 119、INT. BENJAMIN'S ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 119、INT. BENJAMIN'S ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin lies in bed in a cold room, gazing out at a snowy night, reflecting on a particular sleepless night.
document_metadata.source_title: 119、INT. BENJAMIN'S ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - NIGHT,

chunks.content: Benjamin, in his small room, cold air blasting through the windows, looking out the window into the snowy night... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) And longer nights... He lays on his bed looking out at the dark sky... the snow falling... . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) One particular night... when I was having trouble sleeping...

document_metadata.doc_title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin and Elizabeth, bonding over tea, share stories of travel and home—she's a well-traveled minister's wife; he's from New Orleans—finding solace in their late-night connection.
document_metadata.source_title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: Benjamin trudges down the stairs, stepping tentatively into the empty lobby... He slows, seeing ELIZABETH ABBOTT in her bathrobe, sitting, alone and lonely... and it's not the first time for her... BENJAMIN I'm sorry... I can't sleep... She's quiet... She finally looks up... but doesn't say anything... There's an awkward moment... exacerbated by the stillness of the hotel in the middle of the night... BENJAMIN (CONT'D) I was going to make some tea... would you like some? She shakes her head no... He crosses through the empty bar, into an old KITCHEN... He looks for tea... Puts water in a kettle... As he watches the kettle boil... Elizabeth, her arms folded across her chest as if she were chilled, stands by the door... Benjamin, without asking, takes a cup for her... BENJAMIN (CONT'D) Milk...? Honey...? ELIZABETH ABBOTT Some honey, thank you. He finds a large honey jar... and seeing some dead flies in with the sweet syrup he asks... BENJAMIN Do you like flies with your tea? She smiles... for the first time... A thin smile... He starts to stir the tea... Elizabeth stopping him... ELIZABETH ABBOTT You must let it steep for a minute... BENJAMIN Steep? . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT Sit. There's a proper way to make tea. BENJAMIN Where I'm from, they just want it to be hot. She doesn't smile. He gives her a cup of tea... She cradles the cup... They're quiet, drinking their tea... two strangers... After some moments... ELIZABETH ABBOTT You're a seaman? I don't mean to be rude... but aren't you rather old to be working on a boat? BENJAMIN There's no age limit... as long as you can do the work... She nods... They're quiet again. She sits at an old wood counter. ELIZABETH ABBOTT You have trouble sleeping? It's an invitation to sit with her... He pulls a stool over sitting across from her... BENJAMIN I didn't know I did... I usually sleep like a baby. Something kept me up. ELIZABETH ABBOTT I never sleep... Well, rarely anyway... He doesn't say anything. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) My father, when he was in his eighties, was so sure he was going to die in his sleep... He would only take naps during the afternoon... so that death couldn't catch him... BENJAMIN Did he? . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT Did he what? BENJAMIN Die in his sleep? ELIZABETH ABBOTT He died sitting in his favorite chair listening to his favorite program on the radio. BENJAMIN (smiles) He must have known something. She smiles at the idea... Another one... that goes as quickly as it's come... And it's quiet again...

metadata.doc_title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,
metadata.title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Benjamin and Elizabeth, bonding over tea, share stories of travel and home—she's a well-traveled minister's wife; he's from New Orleans—finding solace in their late-night connection.
metadata.source_title: 120、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: ELIZABETH ABBOTT My husband's the British Trade Minister. We've been here fourteen months... We were supposed to be going to Peking... but it just never did work out. It never does seem to work out. Have you been to the Far East? BENJAMIN I haven't really been anywhere. I mean outside different harbors. ELIZABETH ABBOTT Where are you from? BENJAMIN New Orleans, Louisiana. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (pure Elizabeth) I didn't know there was another one. Which escapes him. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) I've never been to America. Everywhere else. But not America. Am I missing anything? BENJAMIN (simply, guileless) The Mississippi River. . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) And she told me all the places she had been, and what she had seen... ELIZABETH ABBOTT I can tell you what bars look like in places all over the world...BUTTON'S (V.O.) And we talked until just before the dawn...

document_metadata.title: 121、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin and Elizabeth share quiet, nightly meetings before parting to their separate rooms, continuing a routine of secret, intimate moments in the stillness of night.
document_metadata.source_title: 121、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,

chunks.content: The first hint of daylight... ELIZABETH ABBOTT Thank you for the tea... She leaves as quietly as she entered... Benjamin remains standing for a moment...then shuts the light off behind him. BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) ...And we went back to our rooms... to our separate lives... And as he goes back up the quiet stairs... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) And every night... we would meet in the middle Of the night...

document_metadata.doc_title: 123、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - BEFORE DAWN,
document_metadata.title: 123、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - BEFORE DAWN,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin and Elizabeth share a quiet moment drinking tea, reflecting on the comfort of loved ones being safe and asleep.
document_metadata.source_title: 123、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - BEFORE DAWN,

chunks.content: Elizabeth and Benjamin quietly talking... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) A hotel in the middle of the night can be a magical place... And we see the empty front desk and tiny silver bell... The vacant lobby, with its musty old rugs... The open elevator, waiting... The dining room, with its crisp white tablecloths. . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) A mouse stopping and running and stopping... A mouse crossing the lobby floor doing just that... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) A radiator hissing. A sink dripping. A floor creaking. A curtain blowing. We see and hear it all... All the little sounds, a symphony, that make up life in a hotel in the middle of the night...

metadata.doc_title: 123、INT. KITCHEN, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - BEFORE DAWN,

document_metadata.doc_title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,
document_metadata.title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth Abbott reaffirms her love for her husband, praising his intelligence and consideration, and clarifies that choosing to live in his shadow was her decision, not his fault, before leaving Benjamin.
document_metadata.source_title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,

chunks.content: Daylight starts to creep in... she gets up, about to go... she slows... ELIZABETH ABBOTT I may have given you the wrong impression. BENJAMIN The wrong impression? ELIZABETH ABBOTT You must think I don't love my husband. BENJAMIN Why do you say that? ELIZABETH ABBOTT Married women don't usually sit with strange men in a hotel in the middle of the night. I certainly don't.

metadata.doc_title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,
metadata.title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,
metadata.summary: Elizabeth Abbott reaffirms her love for her husband, praising his intelligence and consideration, and clarifies that choosing to live in his shadow was her decision, not his fault, before leaving Benjamin.
metadata.source_title: 125、INT. KITCHEN - "WINTER PALACE" - RUSSIA - DAYBREAK,

chunks.content: BENJAMIN (honestly) I don't know what married women do or don't do. ELIZABETH ABBOTT Let's get one thing straight. I love him very much. I happen to think he is one of the smartest and most considerate men I ever met. It is not his fault I decided to spend my life in his shadow.And with that she gets up and leaves... Benjamin, left with that thought...

document_metadata.doc_title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth abruptly leaves after kissing Benjamin, who reflects that it was his first kiss—a moment he will never forget—as she departs, noting her husband will soon be up.
document_metadata.source_title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: Benjamin and Elizabeth in the empty dining room at a table with a white tablecloth... with some wine and cheese... She's laughing now, measurably loosened up... ELIZABETH ABBOTT He started to take his pants off... I'm afraid he misread me completely... He laughs. She looks through her wine glass at him... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) Do you notice how people look better through a wine glass... He holds his up.... looking at her....She moves her glass just looking at him... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) You're a good looking man with or without a wine glass... She picks at the tablecloth with her finger next to his... She puts her finger over his making a cross... . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) We are all just crossing in the night. Sometimes we intersect. She leaves her finger there for a moment... lingering...

metadata.doc_title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Elizabeth abruptly leaves after kissing Benjamin, who reflects that it was his first kiss—a moment he will never forget—as she departs, noting her husband will soon be up.
metadata.source_title: 126、INT. DINING ROOM, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT,

chunks.content: She abruptly moves it away... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) I should go to bed... he'll be up soon. She hesitates... And she kisses him, and then hurries out of the dining room... As Benjamin sits in the empty dining room... the kiss left on his lips... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) It was the first time a woman had ever kissed me. It's something you never forget.

document_metadata.title: 127、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

document_metadata.source_title: 127、INT. THE HOSPITAL ROOM, NEW ORLEANS - DAY, PRESENT

chunks.content: The wind and rain knocking at the window. Daisy silently lying in bed. CAROLINE Are you upset, Mother? She doesn't say anything. Caroline, seeing her feet have come out of the covers, caring, fixes her blanket. CAROLINE (CONT'D) Would you like some socks? Daisy's quiet. CAROLINE (CONT'D) Do you want me to stop reading? Daisy's answer for her is... DAISY It must have been very cold. I'm glad he had somebody to keep him warm. Which Caroline takes as her cue to read on... CAROLINE (after a beat, reading) "I couldn't wait to see her again." .

document_metadata.doc_title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth, noting Benjamin's inexperience, reflects on her youth and her attempt at nineteen to swim the English Channel, savoring the moment with him.
document_metadata.source_title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: Benjamin comes hurrying down the stairs. Elizabeth is waiting, as she normally is, but this time she is dressed... Lipstick and hair done... wearing a fur. . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN (self-conscious) I'm not dressed -- ELIZABETH ABBOTT You're delicious just as you are... She laughs, taking his arm, walking to the dining room as if going to dinner... They sit at a table... which she has set for them... Caviar and Vodka... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) Don't bother with the cheese or the wine here, they're quite common... but the caviar and the vodka are plentiful and sublime... She feeds him a spoonful of the caviar...Unaccustomed to it, he swallows it too quickly... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) Take your time... If you eat it all at once there will be nothing left to enjoy... savor it... She gives him another spoonful... and takes one herself... He takes his time... They both do... savoring it... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) (pouring) Now, a swallow of vodka... Which they do... She laughs... Looking at him...

metadata.doc_title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,
metadata.title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Elizabeth, noting Benjamin's inexperience, reflects on her youth and her attempt at nineteen to swim the English Channel, savoring the moment with him.
metadata.source_title: 128、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) You haven't been with many women have you? BENJAMIN No. Not many. At least none on a Sunday. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (smiles) I feel like I'm with a virgin. She's not far off... And it's a lovely thought... and it makes her think of her youth. . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) When I was nineteen, I tried to become the first woman to swim the English Channel...

document_metadata.doc_title: 129、EXT. THE ENGLISH CHANNEL DAY,
document_metadata.title: 129、EXT. THE ENGLISH CHANNEL DAY,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth Abbott swam for 32 hours across the English Channel, battling strong currents and rain that obscured the shore; she was eventually pulled from the water exhausted, close to the French coast.
document_metadata.source_title: 129、EXT. THE ENGLISH CHANNEL DAY,

chunks.content: And we see just that....Young Elizabeth, in goggles, her body covered with grease, swimming with two escort boats across the English Channel. ELIZABETH ABBOTT'S (V.O.) The current was so strong...that for every stroke I took... I was pushed two strokes back... And we see just that, Elizabeth fighting the current... ELIZABETH ABBOTT'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) I swam for 32 hours... I was only two miles from the French shore... Elizabeth in sight of the lights of Calais...

metadata.doc_title: 129、EXT. THE ENGLISH CHANNEL DAY,

(CONT'D) When I couldn't go any further, and I just stopped... And we see her being taken onto a boat, a blanket wrapped around her...

document_metadata.doc_title: 131、INT. DINING ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 131、INT. DINING ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth and Benjamin share a quiet, intimate moment; she touches his hands and face, he kisses her, but she leaves suddenly, citing the witching hour, leaving him alone.
document_metadata.source_title: 131、INT. DINING ROOM - "WINTER PALACE" - LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: ELIZABETH ABBOTT I never did. As a matter of fact, I have never done much of anything with my life after that... And it's quiet. She touches his rough hand. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) Your hands are very rough... you have grease under your nails... She runs her fingernail along his face... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) I can feel the wind on your face... They look at each other. And this time, Benjamin kisses her. It lingers... She stops herself... ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) I'm afraid it's the witching hour... She quickly gets up... And she's gone. As Benjamin sits in the empty dining room. BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) It took me a long time to go to sleep.

document_metadata.title: 132、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth, holding champagne, meets Benjamin in a borrowed suit; they share a moment of admiration before walking through the empty lobby, discussing comfort in clothing.
document_metadata.source_title: 132、INT. "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - ANOTHER LATE NIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Elizabeth nicely dressed, a bottle of champagne in her hand, sitting anxiously waiting. The elevator doors open. Benjamin in a suit and tie, as handsome as we've seen him steps out. She stands, takes his arm. BENJAMIN Do I look okay? I borrowed it from one of the men. It's his church suit. ELIZABETH ABBOTT You take my breath away. She walks with him, champagne bottle in hand, through the empty lobby... . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) The thing about clothing is, it should make you feel comfortable, then you will be comfortable... Come, let's take a walk...

document_metadata.doc_title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: An elderly couple in a moonlit Russian town reflects on youth and regrets, then silently agrees to a fleeting, rule-bound affair, sealing it with a kiss before walking away together.
document_metadata.source_title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,

chunks.content: Their arms in each other's, their breath showing in the night, they walk through the sleeping Russian town, their shadows in the moonlight. They stop to share a drink from the champagne bottle. They laugh. BENJAMIN I feel so much younger when I'm with you... And it seems he's about to go on... But Elizabeth, flattered, takes it metaphorically... ELIZABETH ABBOTT That's such a nice thing to say. You make me feel years younger, too. I wish I was. I would change so many things. I would undo all of my mistakes. BENJAMIN What mistakes? ELIZABETH ABBOTT I kept waiting, thinking I would do something to change my circumstance... Do something... But I never did... It's an awful waste, you can never get it back... wasted time... They're quiet. She looks at him.

metadata.doc_title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,
metadata.title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,
metadata.summary: An elderly couple in a moonlit Russian town reflects on youth and regrets, then silently agrees to a fleeting, rule-bound affair, sealing it with a kiss before walking away together.
metadata.source_title: 133、EXT. MURMANSK, RUSSIA - DEAD OF NIGHT,

chunks.content: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) (abruptly) If we're going to have an affair, you're never to look at me during the day, we must always part by sunrise, and we can never say \"I love you...\" He's quiet... . CONTINUED: ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) And when it is over I will send you a card that will simply say goodbye... Those are the rules... They stand in the cold. His answer is... BENJAMIN Are you as cold as I am? ELIZABETH ABBOTT (laughs) My god, colder. They stop to finish what's left of the champagne, Elizabeth hurling the bottle. The bottle falling silently into some fresh snow. ELIZABETH ABBOTT (CONT'D) You can't even break a bottle here.They look at each other and they kiss. And without anything else needing to be said, they start back...

document_metadata.source_title: 139、INT. HALL "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - NIGHT TO DAWN,

chunks.content: We see the key going into the door... Benjamin and Elizabeth going inside closing the door behind them... leaving us with the quiet hallway. BENJAMIN'S (V.O.) But each time seemed new and different... And we see them as dawn creeps along the hallway, Benjamin and Elizabeth, leaving the room, not wanting to part, passionately kissing, and as they start to go their separate ways... BENJAMIN (whispering) Elizabeth... She turns. BENJAMIN (CONT'D) (whispers) You should swim the English channel again. And as she laughs to herself and hurries off... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) Until one night... .

He goes back to the lobby, sitting on a lone sofa, waiting for her... A mouse runs across the marble floor, stops, looks at him and runs off... And he sits and waits.

document_metadata.doc_title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,
document_metadata.title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,
document_metadata.summary: Cook Mayes leaves to see his ailing wife; Benjamin volunteers to replace him, and Captain Mike rallies the crew to join the war effort, which they enthusiastically accept.
document_metadata.source_title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,

chunks.content: Snow shrouds the windows. We see Benjamin has fallen asleep on the sofa... There's the distinctive BELLOW of Captain Mike's VOICE. Benjamin wakes... He follows the bellowing to find Captain Mike with the tugboat CREW in the bar... CAPT. MIKE Roosevelt says we all got to do our part! After them Japs attacked Pearl Harbor everyone's got to! The Chelsea's been commissioned to serve in the United States Navy, to repair, tow, salvage and rescue... Anybody don't want to go to war, now's the time to say so... Once you set foot on that boat again, you're in the Navy friend! BENJAMIN (right away) I'll go captain! CAPT. MIKE Easy old timer. (to the men) I'll hold it against no man. But speak up now or forever hold your water.

metadata.doc_title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,
metadata.title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,
metadata.summary: Cook Mayes leaves to see his ailing wife; Benjamin volunteers to replace him, and Captain Mike rallies the crew to join the war effort, which they enthusiastically accept.
metadata.source_title: 141、INT. LOBBY, "WINTER PALACE," RUSSIA - EARLY MORNING,

chunks.content: And the Cook, Prentis Mayes... THE COOK I was planning on talking to you Cap'n Mike... My wife's doing poorly. I'd like to see her one more time... CAPT. MIKE (understanding) You're free to get home any way you can Mr. Mayes. . CONTINUED: And the cook walks off. JOHN GRIMM (always dour) Who do you intend to have cook then? One of the leading causes of death at sea is food poisoning, right after inadequate safety equipment. BENJAMIN I grew up cooking, sir. I'll take the job, if I'm not too old to serve. CAPT. MIKE You a real Johnny on the Spot, Benjamin. I'll take any able bodied mens who wants kick shit out of the Japs and the Huns.And with no one dissenting... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) Then that's it! We's goin' to war, gentlemen! And filled with fervor, they give a cheer.

document_metadata.doc_title: 142、INT. BENJAMIN'S ROOM, "WINTER PALACE" LATER,

document_metadata.source_title: 142、INT. BENJAMIN'S ROOM, "WINTER PALACE" LATER,

chunks.content: Benjamin unlocking the door to his room. An ENVELOPE has been left under the door, he opens it. BENJAMIN'S (V.O.) She had left a note. She wrote, "it was nice to have met you." That was it. And as he stands holding the letter in his room at the small Russian hotel: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) And so, I went to war.

document_metadata.doc_title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Dennis Smith questions pacifism and expresses grim wartime sentiments; Benjamin Button recalls working in the kitchen, overhearing Smith's remarks aboard the tug.
document_metadata.source_title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,

chunks.content: The men on the tug on a dark gray sea.... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) It wasn't the war we expected. We would tow crippled ships... scraps of metal... (MORE) . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) across the high seas... If there was a war, we didn't see it... And what seemed exciting, the idea of war... is tedious... The \"Chelsea\" towing a strange hulking shape on the dark, empty sea... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) There was a man assigned with us... The Chief Gunner loved the Navy, and most of all, he loved America. THE MAN'S (V.O.) There is no other country in the world...! When YOU spell America, A.M.E.R.I.C.A. You're spelling freedom...! We see the young Gunnery Mate, no more than nineteen... sitting at his post on a high caliber machine gun... ready to kick some enemy ass... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.0.) His name was Dennis Smith and he was a full blooded Cherokee... His family had been in America for over five hundred years.

metadata.doc_title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Dennis Smith questions pacifism and expresses grim wartime sentiments; Benjamin Button recalls working in the kitchen, overhearing Smith's remarks aboard the tug.
metadata.source_title: 143、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN, SOMEWHERE - NIGHT,

chunks.content: DENNIS SMITH You have these pacifists. They say they won't fight on conscience. Where would we be if everybody decided to act according to their conscience? CAPT. MIKE (out his Window) Keeps it down, would you chief! He goes back inside... And as they settle into their tasks.. DENNIS SMITH (on his gun, to himself, the last word) Where else can you shoot white people and get away with it... Benjamin's the only one around to hear him... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) I worked in the kitchen...

Pleasant, not interested, just gets up and leaves. JOHN GRIMM There's something not normal about him. As they silently eat, mostly bored... DENNIS SMITH (looking outside) Whoever said "War is hell," doesn't know shit from shinola.

We were towing a British freighter, that had gone dead in the water, 800 miles to Halifax for repair... We see Benjamin and the crew watching the ship on the tow line run out some thousand feet behind them...

document_metadata.doc_title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin sees the dark sea when Captain Mike calls all hands on deck, prompting the crew to rush outside.
document_metadata.source_title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin awake in his bunk, Dennis Smith asleep in the bunk above him. Pleasant Curtis seemingly asleep in his bunk below him... Benjamin looking out at the black sea... and out of the silence Pleasant Curtis for the first time speaks... PLEASANT CURTIS I've been watching you. You seem trustworthy. If something happens to me... could you see this gets to my wife...? He hands Benjamin a folded up handkerchief... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) He had given me all of his pay... he hadn't spent a dime of it... PLEASANT CURTIS If anything happens I want my family to know I was thinking about them, and if I could have, I'd have come back home. And that said he turns back over...

metadata.doc_title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

metadata.source_title: 147、INT. CREW QUARTER, TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: And as Benjamin looks at the dark foreboding sea... suddenly: CAPT. MIKE (OVER) (calls) All hands on deck!!! They bolt from their bunks... Going outside...

document_metadata.doc_title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Captain Mike's tug arrives at a sinking transport with a gaping hole, finding men trapped in burning oil; the vessel vanishes underwater, revealing war's grim toll.
document_metadata.source_title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: Captain Mike stands by the wheelhouse, silently looking at the ocean. They see bodies of men, dead men, floating by them. One and two at first, then three and four, and then more and more until they are moving through a carpet of bodies. Their propeller literally chops up bodies, to the point where they have to veritably shut their engines down. A transport carrying 900 men had been hit by a torpedo. We were first to arrive at the scene.

metadata.doc_title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Captain Mike's tug arrives at a sinking transport with a gaping hole, finding men trapped in burning oil; the vessel vanishes underwater, revealing war's grim toll.
metadata.source_title: 148、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: As the tug arrives at the scene, they see a transport vessel with a gaping hole in its midships, sinking quickly. Fuel oil is burning on the water, creating a hellish landscape. It's then they see the true horror of the men in the water—struggling, trapped in the burning black oil. The sight is overwhelming, a grim testament to the war's devastation.The transport boat silently slips into the water, disappearing under the sea...

document_metadata.doc_title: 149、EXT. TUGBOAT - ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 149、EXT. TUGBOAT - ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: A tugboat moves through smoke after an attack; the crew spots the surfaced U-boat responsible, and Captain Mike orders battle stations as they prepare to confront it.
document_metadata.source_title: 149、EXT. TUGBOAT - ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: As the tug moves through the thick black smoke... Benjamin and the other crewmen watching along the rails... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) There wasn't a sound... Except for the lapping of water, and the tugboat's engines, there isn't... just the silence of death... Something else appears, doming onto the surface like a spectre... the U-BOAT that had reeked this havoc... looking to see the results... Captain Mike sees the sub... CAPT. MIKE (mad as hell) We can't run from the fucker and we can't hide...! There's only one thing we can do...! (and he shouts) Battle Stations...!!! They run to their battle stations...

document_metadata.doc_title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Captain Mike, fatally wounded and covered in blood, dies in Benjamin's arms after reflecting on life and accepting his fate, asking for help to let go.
document_metadata.source_title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: A German submariner, on the conning tower, seeing the Tugboat, turns the .50 caliber machine gun on the tugboat... Benjamin is grazed by a bullet, his forehead cut open, bleeding... Despite the strafing the tug is relentless... The submarine, seeing it is about to be rammed tries to dive... but it's too late... the tugboat ramming the submarine... severing the U-Boat in half. The concussion of the collision has triggered a torpedo in the sinking submarine's torpedo shaft, the torpedo exploding, bursting the submarine, and in the process, blasting away under the stern of the tugboat... the men on the stern blown to pieces... Benjamin's literally thrown against the wheel house... He manages to get to his feet, the tug listing, beginning to sink...

metadata.doc_title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Captain Mike, fatally wounded and covered in blood, dies in Benjamin's arms after reflecting on life and accepting his fate, asking for help to let go.
metadata.source_title: 151、EXT. TUGBOAT, ATLANTIC OCEAN - NIGHT,

chunks.content: There's a man's voice... . CONTINUED: And he sees, Captain Mike riddled with bullets, his body covered with blood... Benjamin bends to him... Captain Mike trembling as he lays dying... CAPT. MIKE Look at what they did! They shot holes in me! They shots the hell out my paintin'! His body, his tattoos, like a ripped canvas, is riddled... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) You've seen a lot of things. Tell me it's going to be alright. BENJAMIN You're going to heaven Captain Mike. You're going to heaven. Benjamin sits beside him, his friend Captain Mike, dying. And a light comes in Captain Mike's eyes... an understanding.CAPT. MIKE You can be mad as a mad dawg at the way things wents... You can swear, curse the fates, regret every'ting you ever dids... but when it comes to the end... You have to lets go... He looks in Benjamin's old eyes.... CAPT. MIKE (CONT'D) Give me a hand, old man... And as he holds Benjamin's hand ready to meet his maker...

document_metadata.doc_title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,
document_metadata.title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin, now a sailor, reflects at sea in 1945, witnessing a rare hummingbird near a wreath, symbolizing fleeting life and memory, before returning home at age 26.
document_metadata.source_title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin at the railing of a Liberty Ship. He watches the \"Chelsea\" sink, disappearing under the sea... CONTINUED: BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) men died that day... I said my goodbyes to the Cherokee, Dennis Smith, John Grimm who was right, he was going to die there... I sent Pleasant Curtis' wife his money... I said goodbye to the twin, Vic Brody... He instinctively turns, and sees Rick Brody looking out a porthole, lost without his twin brother... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) And to Mike Clark... Captain of the tugboat \"Chelsea.\" A storage cabinet is opened, a sailor taking out a wreath, from a supply of just such wreaths... BENJAMIN You mind... The Sailor shrugs, giving him the wreath... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) I said goodbye to all the other men... who had dreams of their own... All the men who wanted to be plumbers or singers or insurance salesmen or doctors... or lawyers or Indian chiefs. And suddenly, angrily, he throws the wreath into the water... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) Out here, death didn't seem normal.

metadata.doc_title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,
metadata.title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,
metadata.summary: Benjamin, now a sailor, reflects at sea in 1945, witnessing a rare hummingbird near a wreath, symbolizing fleeting life and memory, before returning home at age 26.
metadata.source_title: 153、EXT. A LIBERTY SHIP, THE NORTH ATLANTIC - DUSK,

chunks.content: Benjamin standing at the rail of the ship... no longer a boy... And a SAILOR standing beside him.... THE SAILOR This don't get fixed... Benjamin's quiet. When suddenly a HUMMINGBIRD comes flying across the water... It circles the wreath, the way Hummingbirds do... and then flies off... BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) ...I'd never seen a hummingbird that far out to sea before... CONTINUED: And as Benjamin stands at the railing, looking at the sea...In the spring of 1945.... when I was 26 years old... I went home...

document_metadata.doc_title: 154、EXT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 154、EXT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin, now a handsome man in his fifties, returns to his childhood home with a suitcase; an old blind dog greets him, and a young girl informs him his mother is preparing supper as he enters the house.
document_metadata.source_title: 154、EXT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin, suitcase in hand, going up the walk to the old house. We're struck by the difference... the old man who had left to see the world has returned a strikingly handsome man in his fifties. The old blind dog, smelling ham, ambles off the porch to meet him. Nothing seems to have changed. An old woman we don't know is rocking on the porch. A black girl, just 14... is hanging out wash... BENJAMIN Is your mother home? THE GIRL She's gettin' supper ready.... He goes up the porch, inside....

metadata.doc_title: 154、EXT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,

document_metadata.doc_title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin returns home after eight years; Queenie, emotional, reveals their bond, mourns Mr. Weathers' death, and expresses joy at Benjamin's return, focusing on his future.
document_metadata.source_title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,

chunks.content: Some old folks are in the front room... Nobody we know... He moves by them into the kitchen... the stovetop smoking and gurgling... He goes into the dining room... Queenie is busy setting the table... He watches her for a moment... BENJAMIN (quietly) Queenie... She turns, seeing him... she drops a plate... QUEENIE Lord have mercy....you're home... She runs to embrace him... We see she's aged... the eight years he's been gone... and the 25 years or so since we've known her... now in her fifties... THE GIRL'S (V.O.) (asks) Who is that mama? The Girl comes inside... curious... . CONTINUED: QUEENIE Your brother, Benjamin... THE GIRL I didn't know he was my brother. QUEENIE (laughs) There's a shit load of things you don't know... But her interest is in Benjamin.... QUEENIE (CONT'D) (studying him) You look like you've been born again... you're younger than the springtime... I think that preacher laid the hands on you brought you a second life... I knew the moment I saw you -- you were special... Every night I got on my knees asking the Good Lord to bring you back safely. Remember what I told you...? BENJAMIN You never know what's comin' for you. And they both share a good laugh at her homily... glad to be together once again.

metadata.doc_title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
metadata.title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,
metadata.summary: Benjamin returns home after eight years; Queenie, emotional, reveals their bond, mourns Mr. Weathers' death, and expresses joy at Benjamin's return, focusing on his future.
metadata.source_title: 155、INT. THE NOLAN HOUSE, NEW ORLEANS - TWILIGHT,

chunks.content: QUEENIE Did you learn anything worth repeating? BENJAMIN I saw a lot of things. She touches the scar, from the bullet, on his forehead. QUEENIE You seen some pain. He nods. QUEENIE (CONT'D) Some joy too? He nods, that too. And she holds him again. . CONTINUED: BENJAMIN Where's Tizzy? QUEENIE Mr. Weathers died in his sleep one night last April. He's sleeping comfortably now in the cemetery on St. James street, God rest his soul... BENJAMIN I'm so sorry... She turns from him so as not to cry.... QUEENIE There's only one or two of them left now... They all just about new... waitin' their turn like everybody else... I am so glad to have you back. Now we got to find you some proper work and get you married right...And as she goes about readying the table for dinner, humming to herself...

document_metadata.doc_title: 157、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT, LATER,
document_metadata.title: 157、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT, LATER,
document_metadata.summary: Benjamin plays piano for a deaf old man in the parlor, unaware of the man's condition, while Queenie informs him he'll stay in Mrs. DeSeroux's former room.
document_metadata.source_title: 157、INT. PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT, LATER,

chunks.content: We see Benjamin playing the piano in the parlor, the particular tune the Woman had taught him... an old man sitting nearby, seemingly listening... Queenie, looking in... QUEENIE You're wasting your time... he's stone deaf... You'll be staying in what was Mrs. DeSeroux's room now, you're too much of a man to stay in the attic anymore. She goes about her business... And as Benjamin goes back to playing the piano for the deaf man... playing for himself...

document_metadata.doc_title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
document_metadata.summary: Mr. Daws is shown being struck by lightning in his truck as Benjamin reflects on change, time, and distance after returning home, sensing a shift within himself despite unchanged surroundings.
document_metadata.source_title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,

chunks.content: We see Mr. Daws, much older now, asleep in an easy chair. Benjamin stands at the familiar window, listening to the silence of the house. BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) It's a funny thing about coming home. Smells the same. Looks the same. Feels the same. Mr. Daws awakens, seeing Benjamin as if he never left. MR. DAWS Did I ever tell you I've been struck by lightning seven times? Once I was sitting in my truck listening to the radio.

metadata.doc_title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
metadata.title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,
metadata.summary: Mr. Daws is shown being struck by lightning in his truck as Benjamin reflects on change, time, and distance after returning home, sensing a shift within himself despite unchanged surroundings.
metadata.source_title: 158、INT. THE PARLOR, NOLAN HOUSE - NIGHT,

chunks.content: And we see just that: Mr. Daws sitting in his truck, getting struck by lightning. BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) You realize what's changed is you. While Benjamin stands looking out the window, the quiet of the house settling around him, a sense of time and distance pressing in despite the unchanged walls and routines.BENJAMIN BUTTON'S (V.O.) (CONT'D) And one evening, not long after I had been back...
